newsitem.title: CROATIA: PLIVA RISES TO 614 KUNA, THIRD RECORD.
newsitem.headline: PLIVA RISES TO 614 KUNA, THIRD RECORD.

text.p: Leading drugs firm Pliva fetched 614 kuna on Friday on Croatia's central bourse, setting its third consecutive record this week, traders said.
Unlike in previous days of heavy trade, Pliva sold only 400 shares by mid-session. One half went for 614 and the rest for 613 kuna each.
"Supply is a bit thin with few sell offers below 650 kuna," said one trader with a large market share.
Another quoted stock, Varazdinska Banka ordinary A-series, was most active, selling 1,500 shares at around 270 kuna -- compared to 276 at close on Thursday.
It was seen as growing further amid strong demand.
Traders also noted renewed interest for Varazdinska's preferred B-series, which climbed to 205 kuna from 180.
Recent record-breaker, Zagrebacka Banka, paused for a breather and high ask prices for the bank's shares made transactions unlikely.
Its ordinary stock was bid 2,650 and 3,000 kuna, compared to Thursday's close of 2,583, finding no buyers by 1030 GMT. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
